interval: [t, t+10) — left-closed, right-open (floor semantics on both sides)
origin: epoch-aligned multiples of 10 s in both paths (floor of an absolute timestamp)
row_assignment: a flow belongs to the window of its START time (CIC Timestamp / first packet), and ALL of its statistics are attributed to that window
rounding: floor, never round-half; no tolerance band
ordering: groupby(..., sort=True) in training; groupby('window_idx', sort=True) in the PCAP path
empty_windows: produce NO row in either path — the window simply does not exist. Downstream, the 10-second contiguity gate rejects any sequence spanning the gap (np.all(diffs == 10) in prepare_multiday_benchmark.py, mirrored by build_sequences in pcap_ingest_v4.py).
first_window: kept as-is; its relative-change row is forced to 0.0
last_window: kept as-is; sequences needing K future targets simply are not formed

timezone.training: naive local timestamps parsed from the CIC CSV Timestamp column; no tz conversion is applied anywhere in the training path
timezone.pcap: absolute UTC epoch seconds from the capture
timezone.note: Both floor to 10 s multiples, so bin WIDTH and boundary RULE are identical, but the two paths are not anchored to the same clock. The CSE-CIC-IDS2018 CSV clock is Atlantic local with the AM/PM marker dropped, which cannot be reconciled with UTC epoch bins without an explicit offset. This matters only when aligning a PCAP window to a dataset window; it does not change any feature value.
